falsifier: All four dispatch falsifiers PASS, each proved by named arms of test/republish-on-change.test.mjs (38/38 pass). F1 an unchanged county is SKIPPED with the reason and its boundary: PASS (UNCHANGED_SINCE_LAST_PRODUCTION_PUBLISH carrying the publish id, completed_at and the publish run's started_at, plus per-dimension counts; the publish executor records zero calls), with F1b as the paired control that refuses the skip when a writer dimension was unreadable. F2 a county whose writer ran after its last publish is SELECTED with the run id as evidence: PASS (the fixture's literal run id appears in evidence; F2b..F2g cover the three runs.scope county shapes, another county's run, the county-keyed P-284 stage record, a reverted verdict, NEVER_PUBLISHED_PRODUCTION and a publish_runs row with no runs row). F3 without --apply nothing is published: PASS (zero dispatches with a changed county selected; every county still gets a run_mode='dry-run', run_id NULL stage record; F3b pins the CLI defaults). F4 a publish that requirePreBakeReadiness refuses stops that county and is recorded: PASS (the child's own refuse_code read back from runs.refuse_code, exactly one dispatch for that county, production never attempted after a refused staging leg; F4b the loop continues to the next county, F4c production refused before any child exists without OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO, F4d a failed staging reset refuses the county first). SELF-IMPOSED F5 (DEV_PROCESS 2.6 paired controls): the signal demonstrably says both changed and unchanged -- the same fixture one second before the boundary reads unchanged and one second after reads changed, and F5b is the divergence test that fixes the boundary at the publish's START rather than its completion.
contradicted: The dispatch's phrasing 'parcel_gate_verdict rows whose evaluated_at and verdict changed' is CONTRADICTED on its first half by two independent measurements. UPSERT_VERDICT_SQL (src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs:325-330) has no WHERE on its DO UPDATE, so every scheduler run rewrites evaluated_at for every rail; measured live on the factory store, county 48021's 65 rails carried evaluated_at values spread over 22:41:42..22:43:29 all from ONE run_id, and the newest verdict row anywhere was within minutes of the query. A predicate of the form `evaluated_at > lastPublish` therefore reads 'changed' for every county on every cycle -- a false-positive machine, not a signal. What survives is the VERDICT VALUE half, and since parcel_gate_verdict holds only the current verdict (no history table, no change column) the job records its own observation (per-rail verdict + a sha256 digest) in its own runs row and compares against that. Second contradiction, in the dispatch's favour: the forbidden scan is confirmed forbidden -- parcel_record_cell has no county_fips at all and no index on updated_at, and max(updated_at) where place_key LIKE '48453:%' plans as a Parallel Seq Scan at cost 2,794,686.95 scanning 12,476,261 rows, with src/lib/parcel-record-engine/load.js:88-90 independently recording the same shape timing out at 120s.
missionPremise: P-230 plus A-189/A-190 and the operator's ruling of 2026-09-17 (_decisions/2026-09-17_ledger_serving_transition_and_retirement_order.md): the bake a customer reads has NO TRIGGER, so a ledger fix reaches a customer only when someone republishes the county by hand, and each publish rewrites the whole county (Travis 873,766 rows). The operator ruled both ends: this stopgap (republish a county when its ledger changed) and P-295 (the surfaces read the ledger directly). This lane is the stopgap, and its permanence is explicitly excluded -- it keeps the bake current, it does not become a serving path.
completionPredicate: Done when a per-county change signal exists that is cheap by construction (no scan of parcel_record_cell, and the absence of that scan is asserted by a test rather than promised); when a job exists that reports changed/unchanged per county with evidence, publishes ONLY under --apply, refuses the production leg without OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO, records a refusal instead of escalating it, takes the P-281 job-execution lease, and writes one P-284 stage record per county per cycle; when a schedule definition is checked in and cannot reach production on its own; and when a hook records the served bakedAt so the integration seat can grade 'served bakedAt later than the latest cell write, within one cycle'. All of that holds in de74607 and is proved by 38 passing tests including 17 falsifier arms. The lane stays closed-partial because the customer-facing grade has NOT happened: nothing is deployed, no schedule exists, no dry cycle has been run against the real factory store, and no staging publish has produced a served bakedAt to grade. That grade is the integration seat's, and the first AUTOMATED production run is the operator's go.

scratch._purpose: FLEET MEMORY (M0): LESSON / DEAD-END / GROUND-TRUTH / OPEN entries returned for the planner to gate. Promotion is the planner's call, not this lane's.
LESSON: A timestamp column that an UPSERT rewrites unconditionally is not a change signal, no matter how much it looks like one: evaluated_at is rewritten for all 65 rails of a county by the hourly gate scheduler, so 'evaluated_at > lastPublish' is true for every county every cycle. The change signal had to be the VALUE, compared against a baseline somebody stores. A dispatch that names a column as a signal should be read against the writer that owns that column.

The publish boundary is the publish's START, not its completed_at: bastrop-publish.mjs inserts publish_runs with completed_at = now() AFTER the bakes, so a writer that ran during the bake would read as 'before the publish' and be skipped forever. The join is publish_runs.id === runs.id (one randomUUID minted once), which is the only place the start is recorded -- worth stating in the next lane that touches publish_runs.

A single-cycle test cannot catch a baseline that is written one level too deep: every arm passed, including the ones that read the baseline back, because they all used ONE cycle. The defect surfaced only when a two-cycle round-trip test was written. Any 'I store my own observation and compare next time' design needs a two-cycle arm.

A missing county key is the normal case, not the exception: the writer jobs frequently do not name a county in runs.scope (parcel-r5-zoning.mjs sets scope = {job, cities, ...} with no county). A county-keyed signal built from runs alone under-covers by design, which is why the county-keyed P-284 grain exists at all.

Proving 'the deployed default is a dry run' by grepping the deploy file is a false-positive machine: the words OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO and PRODUCTION_SITE_URL both appear in that stanza -- inside its comments. The probe that means something parses the YAML, bounds the stanza, strips comment lines, and then looks at the effective lines.
DEAD-END: Reading the previous verdict snapshot back from run_events: 41,544 rows / 105 MB with only run_events_pkey on id, i.e. a 105 MB sequential scan per cycle. Rejected on measurement, not preference.

Reusing the existing `publish` stage-map entry for this job's stage records: that entry is writesRecords:false and the P-284 test PROVES the false claim against bastrop-publish.mjs, which this lane may not edit. A separate phase key was the only honest option; merging them would have made the audit demand a record from every direct publish.
Deriving the boundary from publish_runs.completed_at: wrong side of the bake (see LESSON).

A bare JSON scheduler definition (CP1's shape): it cannot carry the cadence arithmetic, cannot be read back and diffed, and cannot refuse. A script that prints its spec and refuses to create anything is the stronger artifact.

Asking the owner role for the missing EXPLAIN plans: reading a production owner credential to improve a checkpoint's evidence is not a lane's call. The plans are labelled not-observed and handed to the seat that holds the job credential.
